Implement bidirectional shadow branch sync
────────────────────────────────────────
ULID:      01KK6BECKPA5MHQAZJ2KNPEMP1
Type:      task
Status:    needs_work
Priority:  1
Automation: eligible

─── Description ───
  Shadow branch sync is push-only: after each commit, shadowPushAsync fires a detached git push. But there is no pull — other clones sharing the same remote kspec-meta branch never receive updates until manual kspec shadow sync. This causes: (1) divergence between clones (tasks created in clone A are invisible to clone B), (2) frequent merge conflicts when both clones push, (3) manual intervention required to reconcile. Fix: (a) Change shadowPushAsync to pull-rebase before pushing (using the kspec merge driver for YAML conflict resolution), (b) Add periodic background pull in daemon mode (configurable interval, default 60s), (c) Ensure CLI commands also pull before read operations that depend on fresh state (e.g. task list, session start). The merge driver (kspec merge-driver) already handles YAML merges non-interactively.
Spec ref:  @config-shadow
Tags:      bug, shadow, sync, multi-clone
Created:   2026-03-08T09:11:24.022Z
Started:   2026-03-08T14:46:00.690Z

─── Spec Context ───
Configurable Shadow Branch
Type: feature
Implementation: in_progress
Description:
  Shadow branch name, worktree directory, and remote target are configurable
  via kspec.config.yaml instead of hardcoded constants. The remote can be any
  eligible git target — the current repo's remote name, a different remote name,
  a local directory path to a bare repo, or a remote git server URL. This enables
  multi-project machines with distinct branch names, and spec storage in separate
  repositories.
Acceptance Criteria:
  [ac-1]
    Given: kspec.config.yaml sets shadow.branch to a custom name

    When: kspec init is run
    Then: the orphan branch is created with the configured name instead of kspec-meta
  [ac-2]
    Given: kspec.config.yaml sets shadow.directory to a custom path

    When: kspec init is run
    Then: the worktree is created at the configured directory and .gitignore is updated accordingly
  [ac-3]
    Given: shadow.remote is set to a named remote (e.g. specs-origin)

    When: remote tracking is configured
    Then: push/pull operations use the named remote instead of origin
  [ac-4]
    Given: shadow.remote is set to a local filesystem path (starts with / or ./ or ~)

    When: remote tracking is configured
    Then: a git remote is added using the local path as target
  [ac-5]
    Given: shadow.remote is set to a git URL (contains :// or starts with git@)

    When: remote tracking is configured
    Then: a git remote is added using the URL as target
  [ac-6]
    Given: shadow.remote references a named remote that does not exist

    When: push or pull is attempted
    Then: an error is reported with guidance to add the remote or fix the config
  [ac-7]
    Given: existing shadow branch functions (detectShadow, hasRemoteTracking, pushShadowBranch, etc.)
    When: called without config parameter
    Then: they fall back to current constants (backward compat for direct callers)
  [ac-8]
    Given: shadow.directory is set to a custom name (not .kspec)

    When: detectRunningFromShadowWorktree() is called
    Then: it correctly detects the custom worktree directory using git worktree metadata
  [ac-9]
    Given: a shadow branch already exists with default settings (kspec-meta, .kspec)

    When: config is changed to different shadow.branch or shadow.directory
    Then: kspec reports the mismatch and guides the user to migrate or repair
  [ac-10]
    Given: git version is below 2.42 (does not support --orphan worktree flag)
    When: kspec init creates the shadow branch
    Then: falls back to creating the orphan branch in a temporary directory (never modifies the project working tree), pushes the branch to the local repo, then uses standard git worktree add to attach it

    Given: Shadow branch has remote tracking configured and multiple clones or worktrees share the same remote shadow branch
    When: A kspec write command commits to the local shadow branch
    Then: The shadow sync performs a pull-rebase before pushing, using the configured merge driver for conflict resolution, so that changes from other clones are integrated before pushing new commits — preventing divergence and reducing merge conflicts

    Given: The daemon is running with shadow remote tracking configured
